question: With one source label and product-name ROI, can a fixed method locate missing-name repairs in full target ads while preserving an already-printed control?

cases.role: known actual missing-name failure from Run 22
different-view existing ad with a controlled name deletion; not a new real failure
existing ad with visible name; expected unchanged

fixed: Source image and once-only source regions; full target ads; SIFT/homography method and common thresholds; existing geometry and scene.
changed: Replace per-target manual quadrilaterals with automatic feature alignment and conservative blank-region detection.

alignment.method: SIFT from source label excluding padded name ROI; mutual ratio matches; RANSAC homography

presence.method: Rectify target to source frame; dark-ink occupancy in padded expected-name region; no OCR or semantic correctness claim.

gate.proceed: Both omission cases visibly restored in a reasonable location without new surrounding defects, zero changes outside ink support, and normal control pixel-identical. Small feasibility signal only.
gate.conditional: Only one view/scale works: restrict scope to demonstrated cases; do not claim general automatic restoration.
gate.stop: No repair succeeds, unsafe placement, normal-control damage, or repeated per-target manual alignment: stop this automatic method and retain manual surface assistance.
gate.next: Gate 2 only if a structurally acceptable novel-view product cut is independently available. Surface results do not clear Run 19–21 structural failures.

limits: Second omission is synthetic and easier than arbitrary real generation errors
Curved label approximated by local homography
No OCR; an ink-preserving decision does not verify wording
Preparation-only deletion rectangle is isolated from the automatic pipeline
No per-target target-position parameters or threshold tuning after outputs
reporting: Always include result, gate verdict, and next step.
